title: Hiddo and Ahijah likewise wrote what remains as 1 Kings
source_text: VI. Idem etiam dicimus de libris Hiddo Videntis, & Ahiae Scilonitae, qui memorantur 2 Chron. 9. ubi Salomonis gesta dicuntur scripta fuisse in libris Nathan Prophetae, & in Prophetia Ahiae Scilonitae, & in visione Hiddo Videntis. Etenim videntur illi scripsisse librum primum Regum, qui tertius Regum dicitur in versione vulgata. Nullius enim quidem scriptoris nomen praefert, sed aliis non potest commodius tribui, quam Prophetis illorum temporum.
pass_a_gloss: We say the same also of the books of Iddo the Seer and Ahijah the Shilonite, which are mentioned in 2 Chronicles 9, where Solomon's deeds are said to have been written in the books of Nathan the Prophet, and in the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite, and in the vision of Iddo the Seer. For they seem to have written the first book of Kings, which in the Vulgate version is called the third of Kings. It bears indeed no writer's name, but it cannot more fittingly be ascribed to others than to the Prophets of those times.
pass_b_english: Same move for Iddo and Ahijah in 2 Chron. 9: Solomon's acts credited to Nathan, Ahijah, and Iddo's vision.
Those writings look like 1 Kings, Vulgate 3 Kings — anonymous, yet best ascribed to the prophets of that age.
So again: not vanished canonical books, but books we still read under other titles.

choices.why: Same figure as Rome's Addo in II.
